propositions: A configured provider is silently dropped for any model id containing a colon because _resolve_target treats any ':' in the model as already-qualified, so canonical versioned Bedrock ids like 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0' lose the configured 'bedrock' provider.

The failure surfaces late as an INDETERMINATE/BLOCK gate with a misleading error naming a fragment of the model id ('us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1') as an unknown provider, contradicting the operator's configured provider.

The fix routes both _resolve_target and infer_provider through one shared split_provider_qualifier helper and checks an explicitly configured provider FIRST, before scanning the model string, so punctuation in a model id cannot overrule it.
A conflicting configured-provider and inline qualifier pair raises LLMConfigError rather than silently picking a winner, and no silent fallback to a default provider is introduced.
The qualified/unqualified decision should be made against the registered provider set (delegated to child 7b22), giving an unknown-provider diagnostic that a shape-based test cannot provide.
Existing fail-closed gate behavior on genuine outages is preserved and unversioned Bedrock aliases resolve byte-for-byte unchanged for back-compat.
